defects.title: An interrupted write leaves a stray temporary file beside DATA_FILE that is never removed, not even at the next startup
defects.repro: DATA_FILE=<work>/ledger.json PORT=<free port> node server.js; POST /groups {"id":"g","members":["Ann","Bob"]}; from 8 clients loop POST /groups/g/expenses {"payer":"Ann","cents":2,"split":"equal"}; SIGKILL the server after ~200 ms; ls -a the directory; start again with the same DATA_FILE, GET /groups/g/balances, stop; ls -a again. 5 rounds per product.
defects.expected: Stray temporary files from an interrupted write removed at startup (or never left), so the data directory does not accumulate copies of the ledger
defects.note: Both reports describe the same behaviour (orphan <DATA_FILE>.<uuid>.tmp after a SIGKILL mid-write, kept after restart). Severity low kept. Observed strays were all 0-byte files (the kill landed between open and write), not ledger copies as p47737c#1 described; DATA_FILE itself always parsed and was complete, so the effect is directory clutter only. pc5ec3e names its temporary files .expenses-<uuid>.tmp (hidden).

p47737c.observed: 5 rounds (group g [Ann,Bob]; 8 keep-alive clients looping POST /groups/g/expenses {payer:Ann,cents:2,split:equal}; SIGKILL after 200 ms; ls -a; restart with same DATA_FILE, GET balances, SIGTERM; ls -a). Stray ledger.json.<uuid>.tmp left after the kill and still present after the restart in 1 of 5 rounds (rounds 3); every stray found was 0 bytes. ledger.json parsed in 5 of 5 rounds and after restart Ann's balance was 812/926/997/952/920 against 811/925/997/952/919 acknowledged expenses (no acknowledged expense lost). Server code has no startup cleanup of temporary files.

defects.title: A group with a very long id is created (201) but can never be used: every group route answers 431 or drops the connection
defects.repro: Start the server with a fresh DATA_FILE. POST /groups {"id":"<20,000 x characters>","members":["A","B"]}; then GET /groups/<id>/balances, POST /groups/<id>/expenses {"payer":"A","cents":100,"split":"equal"}, GET /groups/<id>/settlements, and POST /groups with the same id again. Repeat with a 100,000-character id (and 1,000 and 8,000 as controls).
defects.expected: Either refuse ids too long to address (400) or keep every group that got 201 reachable by all three routes.
defects.note: Same on all three products: none limits id length, and Node's default 16 KB header limit makes the path unreachable.

p47737c.observed: POST /groups with a 20,000-character id and members [A,B] -> 201 and the id is written to DATA_FILE; GET /groups/<id>/balances, POST /groups/<id>/expenses and GET /groups/<id>/settlements -> 431 each; a second POST /groups with the same id -> 409. With a 100,000-character id: 201 on create, then every group route -> connection reset (ECONNRESET), re-create -> 409. Ids of 1,000 and 8,000 characters work on all routes (200/201/200). Server keeps serving other requests afterwards (POST /groups id "ok" -> 201). No id length limit in the code.
